comments: Rubric 5 (internal consistency): the decision to move data loading into `[view]/+page.ts` (universal load) and return an un-awaited `event.fetch(...)` promise claims this 'preserves the existing {#await content} streaming/skeleton contract.' It doesn't. SvelteKit's promise-streaming (the chunked `text/sveltekit-data` flush) is implemented only for **server** load nodes — confirmed in `node_modules/@sveltejs/kit/src/runtime/server/data/index.js`, where only `load_server_data` output goes through `server_data_serializer_json`/`chunks`. A universal load's promise gets no such treatment: during SSR, Svelte's `{#await}` simply renders the pending branch synchronously, and the universal load then re-runs a second time in the browser after hydration (this is normal SvelteKit behavior for `+page.js`), firing a second `event.fetch`. So for requirement 7 (direct URL access), the SSR response will always render only the skeleton — real content shows up only after a second client-side round trip — a genuine regression from today's true SSR-streamed content that the plan neither flags as a tradeoff nor accounts for elsewhere.

Rubric 4 (verifyCommands gap): the plan justifies skipping automated coverage of the goto-on-click / URL-derived-activeTab wiring (spec requirements 4 and 5, arguably the riskiest new logic) by asserting 'no unit-test infrastructure in this repo currently mounts a +page.svelte... confirmed: no +page.svelte.spec.ts exists anywhere in src/routes.' That's factually wrong — `src/routes/page.svelte.spec.ts` already does exactly this, rendering `./(app)/+page.svelte` via `vitest-browser-svelte`'s `render()`. Combined with the `vi.mock('$app/navigation', ...)` technique the plan itself references for the cache-store test, a real automated test asserting `goto` (not `invalidateAll`) fires with the correct URL on tab click is achievable and should be added to `verifyCommands` instead of relying solely on manual click-through.
